memoryAids.title: Neuropsychological Tests
memoryAids.content: **Task-demand map:** Trail Making A emphasizes visual scanning, sequencing, and speed; Trail Making B adds alternating-set demands. Wisconsin Card Sorting examines learning from feedback, concept formation, and shifting, with perseverative responding only one score. Naming, clock drawing, finger tapping, and Wechsler subtests sample different language, visuospatial, motor, attention, memory, or reasoning demands. A task is not a one-to-one brain-region detector, and B-minus-A is not a stand-alone diagnosis of executive dysfunction. Interpret with current manuals, appropriate norms, sensory and motor status, language, education, fatigue, validity evidence, history, and converging measures.

memoryAids.title: Exposure & Response Prevention (ERP)
memoryAids.content: **ERP is collaborative exposure plus response prevention for OCD.** Build a shared formulation and hierarchy; approach external or internal triggers in a planned, safe, consent-based way; and refrain from or reduce the linked compulsion, ritual, avoidance, or reassurance/safety behavior long enough to learn something new. Distress may rise, fall, fluctuate, or remain present. Benefit is not limited to "anxiety must habituate"; inhibitory learning and expectancy violation emphasize learning that feared outcomes are less certain or more manageable than predicted. Tailor pacing, accessibility, risk assessment, developmental context, and support; response prevention is not coercive blocking.

memoryAids.title: EMDR — Eye Movement Desensitization
memoryAids.content: **EMDR uses eight protocol phases: History, Preparation, Assessment, Desensitization, Installation, Body scan, Closure, Re-evaluation.** The sequence is a retrieval map, not a do-it-yourself script. EMDR is a trauma-focused psychotherapy with evidence and guideline support for PTSD when delivered with a validated manual by a trained clinician with appropriate supervision. During processing, a person attends to a target memory while receiving alternating bilateral stimulation, commonly eye movements but sometimes taps or tones; preparation, distress-management skills, monitoring, closure, and reevaluation are integral rather than optional extras. The Adaptive Information Processing account is EMDR's theoretical model, not a proven fact that eye movements mimic REM sleep. Current evidence supports the treatment package for PTSD, while the mechanism of action and the incremental role of bilateral stimulation remain debated and under study. Recommendation strength, timing, session number, and fit vary across guidelines, populations, trauma histories, comorbidities, accessibility needs, patient preferences, and response. Do not generalize "effective for PTSD" to every trauma-exposed person, every disorder, or every delivery format, and do not conclude either that eye movements are uniquely curative or that they are known to be unnecessary.

memoryAids.title: Behavioral Activation
memoryAids.content: **Behavioral activation process:** Collaboratively monitor links among activities, context, mood, avoidance, and valued or reinforcing consequences; then test planned, feasible activities and problem-solve barriers. It is not simply telling a depressed person to stay busy or exercise, and immediate pleasure is not the only target. Risk assessment, functional analysis, pacing, disability and resource context, values, comorbidity, and outcome monitoring shape implementation.

memoryAids.title: Paradoxical Intention
memoryAids.content: **Paradoxical intention:** In selected formulations, a person deliberately approaches or exaggerates a feared response to alter anticipatory anxiety and the struggle to suppress it. Evidence is indication-specific, and the intervention is not a contest in which the therapist wins. It requires a clear collaborative rationale, consent, competence, risk assessment, cultural fit, and monitoring. Examples involving insomnia or anxiety are not self-treatment instructions and do not apply automatically to psychosis, suicidality, or every symptom.

memoryAids.title: Evidence-Based Treatment Pairings
memoryAids.content: **Evidence-based practice is not a one-disorder/one-brand lookup table.** Integrate the best available research with clinical expertise and the person's characteristics, culture, preferences, goals, access needs, comorbidity, risk, setting, and prior response. Exam pairings can identify well-supported options: exposure-based methods for many anxiety presentations, ERP for OCD, behavioral activation or structured psychotherapies for depression, and trauma-focused psychotherapies for PTSD. Medication, combined care, family or systems work, and level of care may also be indicated. "Most effective," "gold standard," and "CBT works for everything" require a defined population, comparator, outcome, time point, harms, and evidence source. Shared decision-making, competence, monitoring, and revising a nonbeneficial plan remain essential.

memoryAids.content: **Developmentally responsive medium:** Play therapy uses play, toys, stories, art, and relationship within a defined model to support communication and therapeutic work when verbal abstraction may be limited. Child-centered, cognitive-behavioral, filial, and other approaches differ. Play is not inherently diagnostic or curative, and symbolic meaning cannot be read from one act. Assessment, caregiver involvement, consent and assent, culture, safeguarding, competence, goals, and outcome monitoring matter.

memoryAids.title: Reliability Types
memoryAids.content: **Precision depends on the intended score use:** Internal-consistency coefficients concern relations among item responses; test-retest evidence concerns temporal stability; interrater evidence concerns agreement or consistency among raters; alternate-form evidence concerns form comparability. A high coefficient does not prove validity, unidimensionality, fairness, or individual-score precision. Report the coefficient, design, interval, sample, conditions, uncertainty, and relevant standard error for the intended interpretation.

sourceDetails.organization: AERA, APA, and NCME

memoryAids.title: Validity Types
memoryAids.content: **Replace "four types of validity" with CLAIM -> EVIDENCE -> ARGUMENT -> USE.** Contemporary standards define validity in relation to how well evidence and theory support a proposed interpretation of test scores for a specified use. The test itself does not possess four permanent validity badges. **Content evidence** asks whether tasks adequately represent the intended domain. **Response-process evidence** asks whether respondents and scorers use the processes the interpretation assumes. **Internal-structure evidence** examines dimensionality and relationships among items or components. **Relations-to-other-variables evidence** includes convergent, discriminant, concurrent, predictive, and group-difference patterns when relevant. **Consequences** require examining intended and unintended effects, while recognizing that consequences alone do not establish score meaning. Historical labels such as content, criterion, and construct validity can orient an exam question, but predictive and concurrent are timing distinctions within relations evidence, and convergent, discriminant, and factor-analytic findings are strands of a larger validity argument. "Ecological validity" can ask whether tasks, settings, or inferences generalize to real-world contexts; it is not a coequal fourth psychometric type that validates every use. Reliability or precision is necessary for many interpretations but not sufficient. State the population, score meaning, decision, and conditions; gather the evidence most vulnerable assumptions require; integrate supportive and contradictory findings; and revisit the argument as uses, populations, or evidence change.

memoryAids.title: Sampling Methods
memoryAids.content: **Sampling quality is judged against a target population, frame, selection process, participation, weighting, and intended inference; no method guarantees representativeness.** Simple random sampling gives listed units known, usually equal selection probabilities. Stratified sampling samples within defined strata and can improve precision or subgroup coverage when designed and analyzed correctly. Cluster sampling selects groups of units and requires analysis that accounts for within-cluster dependence. Systematic sampling uses a random start and interval and can be distorted by periodic structure. Nonprobability methods can be useful for many aims but do not support design-based population inference without additional assumptions. Coverage error, nonresponse, exclusions, small subgroups, recruitment mode, and weighting can matter more than the method label. Report who was eligible, reached, enrolled, excluded, and analyzed; probability sampling is not a cure for measurement error or attrition.

memoryAids.title: Factor Analysis
memoryAids.content: **Latent-structure cue:** Exploratory factor analysis estimates patterns without fixing the complete structure in advance; confirmatory factor analysis tests a prespecified measurement model. Principal components summarizes observed variance and is not identical to a common-factor model. Factor number, extraction, rotation, estimator, sample, cross-loadings, fit, and replication matter. A rotated loading pattern does not discover immutable psychological kinds or prove measurement invariance.

memoryAids.title: Chi-Square Test
memoryAids.content: **Categorical-count tests:** Goodness-of-fit compares observed counts with a specified distribution; independence or homogeneity tests compare categorical distributions across variables or groups. Expected counts, independent observations, sampling design, sparse cells, and prespecified categories matter. Statistical significance does not describe effect magnitude or causality. Report cell patterns and an appropriate association measure, and use exact or model-based alternatives when asymptotic conditions are inadequate.

memoryAids.title: Statistical Power
memoryAids.content: **Power is conditional: P(reject H0 | a specified alternative, design, and analysis).** It equals 1 - beta for that specified alternative. Power changes with sample size, effect magnitude, outcome variability/reliability, design efficiency, allocation, alpha, multiplicity, missing data, and the statistical model. Increasing alpha can increase power while increasing Type I error; it is not a free improvement. ".80" is a planning convention, not a universal quality threshold or an 80% chance that a discovered effect is real. Plan with a smallest effect of interest and sensitivity analysis. Post hoc "observed power" calculated from the observed effect is largely redundant with the p value and does not rescue an inconclusive study.

sourceDetails.whyReputable: A peer-reviewed methodological primer that explains power as conditional on effect size, alpha, sample size, and design assumptions.

memoryAids.title: Meta-Analysis Concepts
memoryAids.content: **Meta-analysis statistically synthesizes sufficiently comparable study estimates; it is not automatically the highest or least biased level of evidence.** Define the review question, eligibility criteria, outcome, effect measure, time point, and analysis before pooling. Weighting commonly reflects estimated precision, but a precise biased study remains biased. Examine clinical and methodological diversity, statistical heterogeneity, model assumptions, dependence among effects, influential studies, and sensitivity to defensible choices. A random-effects model does not make unlike studies comparable or erase bias. Funnel-plot asymmetry can have several causes and does not reveal an exact number of missing studies. Missing results, selective outcomes, poor searches, confounding, measurement problems, and publication processes can distort a pooled estimate. Interpret the effect size with its uncertainty, absolute context, harms, applicability, and certainty of evidence; synthesis cannot repair evidence that does not answer the question.

memoryAids.content: **Competence is task and context specific:** Education, training, supervised experience, consultation, study, and appropriate experience support competence; new populations, technologies, languages, disabilities, emergencies, and legal roles may require additional preparation. An urgent service need can alter what limited assistance is permissible, not erase limits. Self-confidence, licensure title, or one course does not establish competence. Monitor outcomes and impairment, document reasoning, and arrange referral or consultation when indicated.

Pro bono service is encouraged as a contribution, not a fixed quota in the Ethics Code. Nonpayment does not automatically authorize abandonment, disclosure, or withholding emergency care.

memoryAids.title: Dissociative Disorders
memoryAids.content: **Dissociative disorder distinctions:** Dissociative identity disorder involves identity-state disruption together with recurrent memory gaps beyond ordinary forgetting. Dissociative amnesia centers on autobiographical memory loss that is inconsistent with normal forgetting; fugue is a specifier involving apparently purposeful travel or bewildered wandering, not a separate diagnosis. Depersonalization means detachment from self, while derealization means unreality or detachment from surroundings; reality testing remains intact in depersonalization/derealization disorder. These experiences also occur transiently and in trauma, panic, substances, seizures, sleep disruption, and other disorders, so structured differential assessment is essential.

memoryAids.title: Somatic Symptom vs Factitious vs Malingering
memoryAids.content: **Do not infer intent from unexplained symptoms:** Somatic symptom disorder concerns disproportionate, persistent thoughts, feelings, or behavior around distressing physical symptoms; symptoms may accompany a medical condition and are not intentionally produced. Factitious disorder involves deliberate falsification or induction with deception but without an obvious external reward. Malingering is intentional symptom production for an identifiable external incentive and is not a mental disorder. The old shortcut of "real, sick role, profit" is incomplete: motives can be unclear, medical illness can coexist, and high-stakes conclusions require records, examination, collateral data, response-validity evidence, and a nonpunitive safety-focused approach.

memoryAids.title: Eating Disorders
memoryAids.content: **Eating-disorder recognition:** Anorexia nervosa involves restriction leading to significantly low weight together with fear of weight gain or persistent behavior interfering with weight gain and altered weight or shape experience. Bulimia nervosa involves recurrent loss-of-control binge episodes with recurrent compensatory behavior and overvaluation of weight or shape, outside an anorexia-only course. Binge-eating disorder involves recurrent distressing loss-of-control binges without the regular compensatory pattern. ARFID is not driven by weight or shape concerns. Appearance and body size do not determine diagnosis or medical risk; assess behavior, cognition, frequency, course, nutrition, vital signs, laboratory risk, suicide risk, culture, and differential causes.

memoryAids.title: Substance Use Disorder Criteria
memoryAids.content: **SUD criterion domains:** The 11 features are organized as impaired control, social impairment, risky use, and pharmacologic adaptation. Meeting 2 or 3 within 12 months is mild, 4 or 5 moderate, and 6 or more severe for a specific substance class. Count the actual substance-linked pattern, impairment, course, and exclusions rather than any use or one consequence. Tolerance and withdrawal alone during appropriate prescribed use do not automatically establish a disorder, and some substance classes lack a defined withdrawal syndrome. Intoxication, withdrawal, substance-induced disorders, hazardous use, and SUD are related but distinct decisions; use the current substance-specific criteria and a qualified assessment.

memoryAids.title: Sleep-Wake Disorders
memoryAids.content: **Sleep differential starts with timing, opportunity, and objective risk:** Chronic insomnia involves repeated difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep despite adequate opportunity, with daytime effect, at least three nights weekly for at least three months. Narcolepsy centers on excessive daytime sleepiness; cataplexy characterizes type 1 but not type 2, and testing is specialized. Obstructive sleep apnea involves recurrent upper-airway obstruction, while central apnea reflects impaired breathing signals; snoring alone is not diagnostic. Parasomnias differ by behavior and sleep timing, but recall is not an absolute shortcut. Review schedule, circadian pattern, substances, medications, breathing, movement, mood, safety, and indications for sleep study.

memoryAids.title: Conversion Disorder (Functional Neurological)
memoryAids.content: **FND is a positive functional diagnosis, not "stress converted into symptoms."** Functional neurological disorder (also called functional neurological symptom disorder) can involve weakness, movement, sensory, speech, gait, or seizure-like symptoms. Symptoms are real and can cause substantial disability. Diagnosis relies on a compatible presentation and positive clinical features showing internal inconsistency or incongruence with recognized neurological disease; it should not rest only on normal tests or the absence of a structural lesion. Psychological stress, trauma, anxiety, or depression may be relevant for some people but is not required, and no single psychodynamic explanation is established. Functional and other neurological conditions can coexist, so a positive FND sign does not make every symptom functional. "La belle indifference" is neither required nor diagnostically specific and should not be used to judge credibility. FND is distinct from intentionally produced symptoms, but intent cannot be inferred from inconsistency alone; malingering involves external incentive and factitious disorder involves deceptive production without that external reward, each requiring evidence beyond a mnemonic. Communicate the diagnosis without blame, explain what positive signs support it, assess comorbid medical and psychological needs, and coordinate individualized treatment that may include education, physiotherapy, occupational or speech therapy, and psychotherapy. The old conversion story is historical context, not a mechanism, lie detector, or treatment plan.

memoryAids.title: Negative Reinforcement vs. Punishment
memoryAids.content: **Classify a consequence with two questions:** Was a stimulus added (+) or removed (−)? Did the future probability of behavior increase (reinforcement) or decrease (punishment)? Positive reinforcement adds and increases; negative reinforcement removes/avoids and increases; positive punishment adds and decreases; negative punishment removes and decreases. Positive/negative do not mean good/bad, and the label depends on observed behavior change—not intention. Escape and avoidance are common negative-reinforcement arrangements; response cost is one form of negative punishment.

memoryAids.title: Extinction & Spontaneous Recovery
memoryAids.content: **Extinction changes contingencies; it does not make behavior "die."** In respondent conditioning, extinction repeatedly presents a conditioned stimulus without the expected unconditioned stimulus. In operant conditioning, the reinforcer that previously followed a response is no longer delivered for that response. Responding may decrease, but the course is not guaranteed to be smooth, complete, or permanent. A temporary increase in rate, duration, intensity, or variability is sometimes called an extinction burst; it can occur, but it is not required and should never be provoked or tolerated without a safety plan. Return of responding can occur after time passes (**spontaneous recovery**), after a context change (**renewal**), after unsignaled reinforcer exposure (**reinstatement**), or when reinforcement resumes (**reacquisition**). These patterns support the view that extinction often creates context-sensitive new learning rather than erasing the original relation. In applied work, first identify the response's function and the actual maintaining reinforcer, teach and reinforce a safe alternative, plan for generalization and maintenance, monitor adverse escalation, and protect assent, dignity, and safety. Withholding attention is not extinction when escape, sensory consequences, access to items, pain, communication difficulty, or another variable maintains the response. "Intermittent is hardest" is only a rough laboratory cue; history, context, reinforcer rate and magnitude, instructions, and the measure of persistence all matter.

memoryAids.title: Classical Conditioning Key Terms
memoryAids.content: **Conditioning terms:** An unconditioned stimulus elicits an unconditioned response without the target training; pairing can make a conditioned stimulus predict that outcome and evoke a conditioned response. Acquisition, extinction, spontaneous recovery, generalization, and discrimination describe measured patterns, not erasure or conscious choice. Timing, contingency, context, prior learning, and biological preparedness qualify simple pairing rules.

memoryAids.title: Stress & Coping Models
memoryAids.content: **Appraisal-and-coping cue:** Transactional models distinguish appraisal of demands and resources from coping efforts. Problem-focused and emotion-focused strategies are not inherently good or bad; fit depends on controllability, timing, goals, culture, safety, and consequences. Avoidance may reduce distress briefly yet maintain some problems, while acceptance can be adaptive without implying resignation. Stress responses are not uniform or purely cognitive.

memoryAids.title: Stereotype Threat
memoryAids.content: **Stereotype threat is a situational hypothesis about performance under identity-relevant evaluative conditions, not a fixed trait or universal explanation for group differences.** In foundational experiments, describing difficult verbal items as diagnostic of ability altered the performance pattern for Black students compared with less identity-threatening framing. Proposed mechanisms include attention to possible confirmation, stress, monitoring, and working-memory demands. Effects depend on population, task, identification, cues, design, outcome, and context; later studies include both supportive findings and null or smaller replications. The construct does not imply that a person endorses a stereotype, that anxiety is the only mechanism, or that framing alone removes structural inequity. Interpret a study from its manipulation, comparison, estimate, uncertainty, and boundary conditions rather than assuming the effect whenever a negatively stereotyped group takes a test.

memoryAids.title: Suicide Risk Assessment
memoryAids.content: **Do not use SAD PERSONS or any demographic checklist as a prediction rule. Use a direct, dynamic safety assessment.** Ask about current and recent suicidal thoughts, frequency, plan, method, access to means, intent, past attempts/self-injury, symptoms and substance use, acute stressors, supports, and reasons for living. Past suicidal behavior is important, but no single factor determines disposition. Current suicidal thoughts, feasible plans/access, intent, inability to maintain safety, rapid change, and clinical context require timely escalation under setting and jurisdiction procedures. Collaboratively create a concrete safety plan and address lethal-means access; a "no-suicide contract" does not establish safety. If danger may be imminent, use emergency resources and do not leave the person unsupported.

memoryAids.title: Crisis Intervention
memoryAids.content: **Crisis care is person-centered, safety-oriented, least restrictive, accessible, and connected to follow-up; it is not a fixed ABC script or session count.** Establish engagement and communication access, clarify the person's view and immediate needs, assess medical and behavioral urgency, suicide or violence risk, substance effects, supports, environment, and access to lethal means, then collaborate on the safest feasible next steps. Use existing strengths and natural supports with consent, address practical needs, create a concrete safety and follow-up plan, coordinate handoffs, and document reasoning. Do not promise confidentiality beyond its limits, use "normal reaction" as a substitute for assessment, or assume returning to pre-crisis functioning is every person's goal. Emergency and jurisdiction procedures govern imminent danger.

memoryAids.content: **Leadership frameworks:** Trait and behavioral approaches ask who leads and what leaders do; contingency models examine fit among style, task, followers, and situation; transactional leadership emphasizes exchanges; transformational leadership emphasizes vision, meaning, and development. These are overlapping research lenses, not fixed leader types or guarantees of effectiveness. Outcome criterion, ethics, power, culture, team composition, implementation, and measurement determine what conclusions are defensible.

memoryAids.title: Performance Rating Measurement Quality
memoryAids.content: **Treat ratings as measurement evidence:** A performance score is interpretable only for its defined job, criteria, raters, occasions, and decision use. Examine score precision, interrater consistency, criterion relevance, construct underrepresentation or contamination, subgroup fairness, range restriction, and consequences. Central clustering or disagreement may reflect scale design, opportunity to observe, real performance variation, or error; it does not by itself identify a named rater bias. Forced distributions create rather than validate a score distribution.

No theory predicts every worker, and satisfaction does not by itself cause performance. memoryAids.content: **Prenatal periods:** Germinal development includes fertilization, early cell division, and implantation; embryonic development includes major early organ formation; fetal development emphasizes growth and maturation. Boundaries are approximate and developmental processes overlap. Exposure effects depend on timing, dose, route, genetics, placental factors, nutrition, health, and co-exposures; a named period does not make harm certain or permit causal inference about an individual child.

memoryAids.title: Piaget's Key Concepts Deep Dive
memoryAids.content: **Piagetian mechanisms:** Schemas organize action or thought; assimilation interprets experience using existing schemas; accommodation modifies schemas; equilibration describes regulation between them. Object permanence, conservation, classification, and abstract reasoning are task-linked achievements, not all-or-none global capacities. Age ranges are historical approximations, and language, familiarity, executive demands, teaching, culture, and revised tasks can change observed performance.

memoryAids.title: Mandated Reporting Details
memoryAids.content: **Mandated reporting is a current-law lookup, not "when in doubt, report."** Determine the jurisdiction, protected population, whether the psychologist's role is covered, reporting threshold, source and timing rules, designated agency, required oral or written follow-up, privilege provisions, and emergency procedures. Child, elder, dependent-adult, intimate-partner, and other reporting duties are not interchangeable. Many child-abuse statutes use reasonable suspicion or reasonable cause rather than proof, but wording and deadlines vary, and not every state names every profession in the same way. Explain confidentiality limits early and, when safe and legally appropriate, tell the client what will be disclosed. Report only what the law requires or permits, consult promptly when uncertain, protect privacy, document the authority and facts, and never let consultation create a prohibited delay.

memoryAids.title: Test Security & Release
memoryAids.content: **Distinguish test data from test materials, then identify authority and risk.** Test data include scores, client responses, and examination notes. Under APA Standard 9.04, psychologists generally provide data pursuant to a client/patient release, with a narrow option to refrain for likely substantial harm or substantial misuse/misrepresentation; absent release, provide only as required by law or court order. Test materials include manuals, instruments, protocols, and questions/stimuli; Standard 9.11 calls for reasonable security efforts consistent with law and contract. Avoid blanket never-release rules.

memoryAids.title: TBI & Neurological Conditions
memoryAids.content: **Use three separate maps: INJURY, SEIZURE CLASS, and COGNITIVE SYNDROME.** **TBI:** A concussion is a mild traumatic brain injury, and loss of consciousness is not required. Acute severity classifications may combine Glasgow Coma Scale scores with loss or alteration of consciousness, post-traumatic amnesia, imaging, timing, and clinical context; a mnemonic or one score is not a diagnosis or prognosis. Symptoms can emerge later, and red flags require prompt medical evaluation. **Seizures:** The 2025 ILAE classification uses four main classes—focal, generalized, unknown whether focal or generalized, and unclassified—then adds classifiers and descriptors supported by the observed chronology and available evidence. Consciousness replaces awareness as a classifier, and observable versus nonobservable manifestations replace the older motor versus nonmotor split. “Grand mal,” “petit mal,” and “simple/complex partial” are legacy terms, and one seizure is not automatically epilepsy. Treatment depends on seizure type, cause, comorbidity, and the person; do not attach one medication to a category by rote. **Dementia:** Alzheimer disease, vascular contributions, Lewy body disease, frontotemporal disorders, and mixed pathologies can produce overlapping and variable presentations. A pattern may guide a differential diagnosis, but no single symptom proves an etiology. Depression, delirium, medications, metabolic conditions, and other disorders can impair cognition, so avoid the imprecise label “pseudodementia” and assess potentially reversible contributors.

memoryAids.title: Test Bias & Fairness
memoryAids.content: **Group score differences, DIF, bias, and fairness are related but not interchangeable.** A mean difference alone does not establish measurement bias. **DIF** flags an item when matched examinees from groups have different response probabilities; it triggers content and construct review but is not automatically proof of bias. Fairness also includes access, standardized and accessible administration, appropriate accommodations, construct-relevant content, valid interpretation across intended groups, opportunity to demonstrate the construct, and responsible consequences/use. Differential prediction and validity require appropriate models and evidence. No instrument is culture-free, and one court ruling or "culture-fair" label does not settle a new use.

memoryAids.title: Interpersonal Therapy (IPT)
memoryAids.content: **Time-limited interpersonal focus:** IPT links current depressive symptoms with one or more focal areas such as grief, role transitions, role disputes, or interpersonal deficits or sensitivities, using assessment, formulation, communication analysis, affect work, and role practice across phases. It is not generic advice to socialize and does not claim relationships are the sole cause of depression. Qualified assessment, risk management, adaptation, consent, and monitoring remain necessary.

memoryAids.title: Criterion-Referenced vs. Norm-Referenced Tests
memoryAids.content: **These terms describe score interpretations, not mutually exclusive kinds of tests.** A criterion-referenced interpretation compares performance with a defined domain, performance standard, or cut score. A norm-referenced interpretation locates performance in a specified reference-population distribution. The same assessment can support both only when evidence justifies each use. A cut score is a decision boundary established through a standard-setting process, not an error-free "absolute" measure of competence; a percentile is meaningful only for its named norm group and date. ASPPB currently recommends 500 as the passing score for EPPP Part 1-Knowledge, but the licensing jurisdiction determines applicable requirements. Do not generalize that number to every EPPP component, historical scale, jurisdiction, or future integrated examination.

memoryAids.content: **Measurement properties guide analysis:** Nominal values label categories; ordinal values add order; interval interpretations assume meaningful equal differences; ratio interpretations also posit a meaningful zero. Real measures can only approximately support these properties, and permissible analysis is not selected by the label alone. Consider the construct, coding, distribution, design, estimand, robustness, and interpretability rather than memorizing that one statistic is universally allowed or forbidden.

memoryAids.title: Gender Identity Development
memoryAids.content: **Keep four concepts separate: assigned sex characteristics, gender identity, gender expression, and sexual orientation.** Gender identity is a person's internal sense of gender; gender expression is how gender may be communicated through appearance, behavior, voice, or other means; sexual orientation concerns patterns of romantic, emotional, or sexual attraction and is not inferred from identity or expression. Sex characteristics include multiple biological dimensions, so avoid treating chromosomes, hormones, gonads, and anatomy as one always-binary variable. Children develop and communicate gender-related concepts in diverse ways and on varied timelines. The classic identity-stability-constancy sequence is a historical cognitive-developmental model, not a test that every child completes at ages 2-3, 4-5, and 6-7, and clothing, toys, interests, or one statement do not establish identity or pathology. Gender diversity itself is not a mental disorder. Distress can arise from incongruence, stigma, rejection, dysphoria, or other concerns and must be assessed in the person's developmental, family, cultural, safety, and social context. Use the person's current language, allow exploration without steering toward a predetermined identity, distinguish support from diagnosis, and avoid assuming that identity fixes orientation, treatment need, or a single developmental outcome.

memoryAids.title: Action Potential Steps
memoryAids.content: **Threshold → rising phase → falling phase → afterhyperpolarization → recovery.** At threshold, voltage-gated sodium conductance rises; sodium-channel inactivation and delayed potassium conductance then drive repolarization. Continued potassium conductance can briefly make the membrane more negative than rest. The absolute refractory period reflects unavailable sodium channels; during the relative refractory period another spike needs stronger input. Myelin permits saltatory propagation between excitable nodes. Exact voltages and timing vary—memorize the mechanism, not one universal number.

memoryAids.title: Neuron Structure
memoryAids.content: **Canonical neuron flow:** Dendrites and soma commonly receive and integrate inputs; axons propagate action potentials toward terminals; chemical synapses often release neurotransmitter onto receptors. This is not an always-one-way law: neurons receive inputs at multiple sites, electrical synapses may be bidirectional, and modulatory and retrograde signals occur. More dendrites do not translate mechanically into "more learning."

memoryAids.title: Glial Cells
memoryAids.content: **Glia support, regulate, defend, and myelinate—do not reduce them to passive “glue.”** Astrocytes help regulate the extracellular environment, metabolism, synapses, and blood–brain-barrier functions. Oligodendrocytes form CNS myelin and can support segments on multiple axons; Schwann cells myelinate PNS segments and support repair. Microglia are resident immune-surveillance and response cells. Ependymal cells line ventricles and participate in cerebrospinal-fluid physiology. Cell counts and roles vary by region; avoid the outdated “glia outnumber neurons 10:1 everywhere” shortcut.

memoryAids.title: Aggression Theories
memoryAids.content: **Aggression is multiply determined; no drive, hormone, transmitter, frustration, or observed model produces it inevitably.** The original frustration-aggression hypothesis was revised: aversive events can produce negative affect and activate aggression-related thoughts or action tendencies, but context, appraisal, learning, inhibition, alternatives, and consequences shape behavior. Social-learning accounts examine modeled behavior, expected outcomes, and reinforcement histories. Biological research examines interacting neural, hormonal, developmental, and environmental processes rather than equations such as low serotonin equals aggression. Distinguish aggressive behavior from assertiveness, anger, thoughts, and lawful self-protection, and specify whether an outcome is reactive, proactive, relational, verbal, or physical. Risk inference requires multiple sources, time course, culture, situational opportunity, protective factors, and direct assessment; a theory mnemonic is not a violence prediction tool.

memoryAids.title: IQ Score Interpretation
memoryAids.content: **For many deviation-IQ scales, 100 is the reference mean and 15 is the reference SD; interpretation still begins with the manual.** Under an approximately normal reference distribution, 115 is about the 84th percentile, 130 about the 98th, 85 about the 16th, and 70 about the 2nd. Those are mathematical approximations, not diagnoses or immutable ranks. Exact percentile tables, composite construction, floors and ceilings, norms, confidence intervals, and descriptive categories depend on the test, edition, age band, and score. Labels such as "superior," "borderline," or "extremely low" are not universal across instruments or editions and can stigmatize; quote the applicable manual and describe functioning in context. An observed score is an estimate with measurement error, so report its confidence interval and avoid treating a cutoff as a perfectly sharp boundary. The 68-95-99.7 rule assumes an ideal normal distribution and does not replace empirical norms, especially in distribution tails. Compare indexes or subtests only with manual-based difference reliability and base rates; a visible gap is not automatically a disorder or special strength. Interpretation integrates referral question, language, culture, disability and access, education, testing behavior, effort and validity indicators when appropriate, developmental and medical history, adaptive functioning, and corroborating data. IQ scores do not measure every valued human ability, reveal fixed potential, establish etiology, or by themselves diagnose intellectual disability, giftedness, learning disorder, or neurocognitive disorder.

memoryAids.title: Privilege & Exceptions
memoryAids.content: **JAFFEE is a federal privilege anchor, not a universal exception list.** In **Jaffee v. Redmond**, the U.S. Supreme Court recognized under federal evidence law a privilege protecting confidential communications made in diagnosis or treatment with licensed psychiatrists, psychologists, and social workers; the Court rejected case-by-case balancing of need against confidentiality. Privilege is an evidentiary protection in legal proceedings, confidentiality is a broader ethical and legal duty governing information, and HIPAA is a federal privacy rule—related concepts, not synonyms. Who holds or may waive privilege, which professionals and communications qualify, and what exceptions apply depend on the forum, jurisdiction, claim, role, and governing statute or case law. Jaffee did not create a nationwide checklist saying that custody, court-ordered evaluation, malpractice, mental-condition claims, or danger automatically defeats privilege, and Tarasoff duties do not automatically "override privilege" everywhere. A subpoena is also not the same as client authorization or a judge's order. When a demand arrives, preserve the material, avoid voluntary disclosure, clarify the legal demand and client position, assert applicable protections, seek qualified legal consultation when needed, and disclose only when authorized or required and only to the permitted extent. In forensic or mandated roles, explain foreseeable limits at the outset and verify current local law.

memoryAids.title: Circadian Rhythms & Sleep Disorders
memoryAids.content: **Use LIGHT -> SCN -> BODY CLOCKS -> TIMED OUTPUTS, not "three built-in clocks."** The suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) is a central circadian pacemaker that receives retinal light information and helps synchronize rhythms across tissues. Melatonin is one output and timing signal: evening darkness usually promotes secretion, but light exposure, dose, timing, age, medications, and individual biology matter. Cortisol has a circadian pattern and often rises around awakening, yet it is not a separate "awakening clock" and a single morning measurement does not diagnose sleep or stress dysfunction. Jet lag and shift work involve misalignment between internal rhythms, sleep opportunity, and the external schedule; circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders require a persistent pattern with clinically important sleep or waking impairment, not merely one late night. Timed light, planned sleep schedules, or melatonin may help selected circadian conditions, but timing is part of the intervention and the same advice is not correct for every disorder. Seasonal-pattern depression is a mood-disorder pattern, not simply "less daylight causes depression," and light therapy needs diagnostic and safety consideration. Sleep architecture changes across development and varies widely: older adults often have less slow-wave sleep and more fragmentation, while infants have more REM than adults. The map supports mechanism recognition; it cannot select a supplement, dose, treatment time, or diagnosis.

memoryAids.title: Adult Attachment Styles
memoryAids.content: **Map adult romantic attachment on two dimensions before naming four prototypes: ANXIETY x AVOIDANCE.** Low anxiety/low avoidance is the secure prototype; high anxiety/low avoidance is preoccupied; low anxiety/high avoidance is dismissing; and high anxiety/high avoidance is fearful. Hazan and Shaver's original adult-romantic extension used secure, avoidant, and anxious/ambivalent descriptions; Bartholomew and Horowitz later proposed four prototypes using models of self and others. Modern self-report research often represents anxiety and avoidance continuously, so category boundaries are teaching conveniences rather than natural diagnostic cutoffs. A person is not simply an "attachment type": scores can differ by relationship, measure, context, and time, and a prototype does not determine self-esteem, behavior, compatibility, or prognosis. Adult romantic self-reports are also not interchangeable with infant Strange Situation classifications or the Adult Attachment Interview, and continuity from one childhood observation to adult romance is probabilistic rather than one-to-one. Drop fixed prevalence percentages and pejorative personality labels. Use the framework to generate questions about closeness, support seeking, rejection concerns, and distancing while assessing the actual relationship and person.

They are influential historical frameworks, not validated biological timetables or diagnostic systems. Do not infer adult symptoms, personality, parenting quality, or treatment needs from a presumed fixation or unresolved stage. memoryAids.title: Culture-Bound Syndromes
memoryAids.content: **Replace "culture-bound box" with three CULTURAL CONCEPTS OF DISTRESS: syndrome, idiom, and explanation.** A cultural syndrome is a locally recognized cluster of experiences; an idiom is a shared way of expressing distress; and an explanation or perceived cause gives meaning to suffering. DSM-5 and DSM-5-TR moved beyond a simple list of "culture-bound syndromes" because culture shapes every clinical encounter, concepts travel across communities, and there is no one-to-one mapping from a cultural concept to a DSM diagnosis. Ataque de nervios, taijin kyofusho, dhat, khyal attacks, and susto are examples for study, not profiles to assign from a person's ethnicity or nationality. Presentation, meaning, prevalence, and help seeking vary within and across communities, and a person's own account can differ from a glossary description. The Cultural Formulation Interview asks how the person defines the problem, understands causes and context, obtains support, encounters barriers, and prefers to receive help; it also examines the clinician-patient relationship. Do not call one concept the "opposite" of a Western disorder, exoticize it, or diagnose it by matching surface symptoms. Ask, contextualize, assess impairment and differential explanations, and document uncertainty.

memoryAids.title: Differential Diagnosis Tips
memoryAids.content: **Differential diagnosis uses discriminating evidence, not slogans:** For depression versus bipolar II, obtain lifetime evidence of hypomanic episodes, collateral change, substances, and medical causes. OCD cannot be reduced to ego-dystonic and OCPD to ego-syntonic because insight and distress vary. Delirium usually has acute or fluctuating attention and awareness changes and needs urgent cause assessment; major neurocognitive disorders are not uniformly gradual or irreversible. Schizoid, schizotypal, and avoidant personality patterns differ in relational interest, eccentric cognition or perception, and rejection sensitivity, but require pervasive longitudinal evidence. Always compare onset, course, context, impairment, exclusions, and the evidence required by each candidate.

memoryAids.title: Flooding vs Implosion vs Graded Exposure
memoryAids.content: **Exposure methods differ in stimulus, intensity, pacing, and learning target; more intense is not automatically more effective.** Flooding traditionally means direct exposure to a high-intensity feared situation without preliminary relaxation. Graded exposure proceeds through collaboratively selected steps. Implosion is a historical imaginal method that amplified feared themes and should not be treated as a routine synonym for contemporary exposure. Modern exposure planning emphasizes informed consent, a shared formulation, feasible approach behavior, expectancy testing, varied practice, reduction of avoidance or compulsions when relevant, and learning that can generalize. Within-session anxiety reduction is not required for benefit, and forcing maximum distress can increase dropout or harm. Match the protocol to the condition, person, culture, medical and safety context, accessibility needs, preferences, evidence, and clinician competence; exposure is not simply endure fear until it disappears.

memoryAids.title: Bowen Family Systems Therapy
memoryAids.content: **Bowen theory cue:** Differentiation, triangles, family projection, multigenerational transmission, emotional cutoff, sibling position, and societal emotional process organize a systems formulation. A genogram supports hypothesis generation, not proof of inherited pathology. Triangles are common relational processes rather than diagnoses, and differentiation is not emotional detachment. Individual symptoms, safety, culture, power, development, and alternative explanations require direct assessment.

memoryAids.title: Reality Therapy — Glasser
memoryAids.content: **Reality therapy and choice theory are historical frameworks that emphasize present choices, needs, relationships, responsibility, and workable action plans; they are not proof that all behavior is freely chosen.** A common WDEP cue is wants, doing or direction, evaluation, and planning. In practice, questions should remain collaborative and account for trauma, disability, neurobiology, coercion, poverty, discrimination, safety, developmental capacity, and limited alternatives. Responsibility language should support agency without blaming people for symptoms or circumstances outside their control. The model's own professional source can define its concepts, but effectiveness claims require independent research, a specified population and outcome, clinician competence, client preferences, and comparison with alternatives. Do not infer that external conditions are irrelevant, that insight or emotion never matters, or that one branded framework is sufficient for every presentation.

The multivariate label does not make a method automatically superior. Clinicians contribute data quality, safety, feasibility, context, and information absent from a model; post-hoc overrides need evidence and documentation. Structured professional judgment is a distinct framework, and every predictive tool requires validation and monitoring in its intended population.

Before proceeding, consider necessity, role conflict, exploitation, objectivity, confidentiality, foreseeable harm, community context, consultation, and alternatives; discuss boundaries and document reasoning. A multiple relationship is not automatically unethical, but scarcity does not make every overlap acceptable or waive competence, consent, records, or termination duties.

memoryAids.title: Psychotropic Medication Classes
memoryAids.content: **AMAS retrieves four broad medication families; it does not prescribe a drug.** **A**ntidepressants include SSRIs, SNRIs, and older agents, but indications overlap and response, adverse effects, age, pregnancy, comorbidity, interactions, prior treatment, and preference affect selection. A fixed "2-6 week onset" is too simple: different symptoms and people improve on different timelines. **M**ood stabilizer is a clinical umbrella that includes lithium and some anticonvulsants or antipsychotics; lithium requires serum-level and organ-function monitoring, and no one drug is universally the gold standard. **A**nti-anxiety medications include antidepressants, buspirone, benzodiazepines, and other agents in selected contexts. Benzodiazepines can produce tolerance, physical dependence, withdrawal, and misuse risk, but "addictive" is not an all-or-none property; buspirone has lower demonstrated abuse/dependence liability, not zero risk or universal superiority. **A**ntipsychotics are not cleanly divided into first-generation "EPS drugs" and second-generation "safe drugs": movement, metabolic, cardiovascular, sedation, and other risks vary by agent and person. Clozapine can be important after inadequate response and carries severe-neutropenia risk. FDA removed the Clozapine REMS in 2025, while label-directed ANC monitoring remains recommended. Use AMAS for recognition only; medication choice, initiation, monitoring, tapering, and interaction management require current labeling and a qualified prescriber.

memoryAids.title: Antidepressant Mechanisms
memoryAids.content: **Antidepressant mechanisms are multi-step and class-specific; depression is not simply too little serotonin or norepinephrine.** SSRIs inhibit the serotonin transporter, SNRIs inhibit serotonin and norepinephrine transporters, tricyclics affect several monoamine and other receptor systems, and monoamine oxidase inhibitors reduce enzymatic monoamine breakdown. Those acute molecular actions occur before typical clinical improvement and do not by themselves explain response. Downstream receptor adaptation, intracellular signaling, neuroplasticity, learning, context, and time are part of current accounts. Benefits, adverse effects, interactions, discontinuation effects, onset, and evidence differ across agents and indications. A mechanism cue cannot diagnose a disorder, predict one person's response, or replace individualized prescribing, monitoring, and safety assessment.

memoryAids.content: **Lobe map with limits:** Frontal regions contribute to motor control and executive functions; parietal regions to somatosensory and spatial processing; temporal regions to auditory, memory, and language networks; occipital regions to vision. Functions arise from distributed networks, vary within lobes, and can reorganize. A symptom or personality style cannot be localized from this mnemonic alone.

memoryAids.content: **Aphasia profiles:** Nonfluent and fluent labels describe patterns across speech production, comprehension, repetition, naming, reading, and writing. Broca- and Wernicke-type prototypes are useful contrasts, but individual lesions and profiles vary and do not map perfectly to one cortical spot. Aphasia is a language disorder, not loss of intelligence; assessment must examine the person's actual modalities and causes.

memoryAids.title: Motivation Theories - I/O
memoryAids.content: **I/O motivation map:** Expectancy theory links effort, performance expectancy, instrumentality, and valued outcomes; equity theory concerns perceived input-outcome fairness; goal-setting emphasizes specific challenging accepted goals with feedback; reinforcement focuses on consequences; self-determination distinguishes autonomous and controlled motivation. These are conditional models, not formulas that guarantee effort. Ability, resources, role clarity, justice, culture, safety, and goal conflict require separate assessment.

Milestone checklists support monitoring, not exact prediction or diagnosis. Multilingual exposure does not itself cause disorder, and vocabulary distributed across languages matters. Hearing, communication access, motor and cognitive development, interaction, culture, and opportunity should inform screening and comprehensive evaluation.

memoryAids.title: Vygotsky's Key Concepts
memoryAids.content: **Supported learning:** The zone of proximal development concerns what a learner can do with appropriate assistance relative to independent performance. Wood, Bruner, and Ross later used "scaffolding" for contingent tutoring functions that support and transfer control; the terms are related but not synonyms. Assistance can involve adults or more capable peers and culturally mediated tools; "more knowledgeable other" is later shorthand, not Vygotsky's named construct. Support must be calibrated, monitored, and faded; completing the task for the learner is not transfer.

NEO-PI-3 measures five broad normal-range trait domains and facets. R-PAS standardizes behavioral responses to inkblots; the TAT elicits stories to picture scenes. Performance-based methods do not directly reveal an unconscious truth, and self-report is not automatically objective or valid. Select and interpret from the referral question, evidence for the intended use, norms, language and culture, response process, qualifications, and convergence with interview, records, and other measures.

memoryAids.title: Neuropsychological Assessment
memoryAids.content: **Assessment is an integrated inference process:** Fixed batteries offer standardized breadth; flexible batteries select measures from the referral question, hypotheses, history, and evolving findings. Both approaches require qualified administration, current manuals, appropriate norms, behavioral observation, records and interview, performance and symptom validity, and attention to language, culture, education, sensory or motor access, medication, fatigue, pain, and emotional state. WCST, Trail Making, naming, construction, and motor tasks have multiple demands and are not lesion locators. Describe strengths, weaknesses, uncertainty, functional meaning, and alternative explanations; one low score, discrepancy, automated printout, or "impairment index" cannot diagnose brain damage or lateralize a lesion.

memoryAids.content: **Yalom therapeutic factors:** Instillation of hope, universality, imparting information, altruism, corrective recapitulation, socializing techniques, imitative behavior, interpersonal learning, cohesiveness, catharsis, and existential factors describe possible change processes. The list is not a rank order, and catharsis or cohesion alone is not sufficient. Factor salience depends on group type, phase, member, culture, leadership, safety, and measurement.

memoryAids.title: Solution-Focused Brief Therapy
memoryAids.content: **Collaborative preferred-future work:** SFBT uses detailed descriptions of preferred outcomes, exceptions, coping, scaling, and small next steps while attending to the client's language and feedback. The miracle question is optional, not a diagnostic test or mandatory script. A strengths focus does not require ignoring risk, trauma, oppression, diagnosis, resources, or causes that matter to the client. Brief does not mean one session or universally sufficient.

memoryAids.title: DBT — Dialectical Behavior Therapy
memoryAids.content: **DBT balances ACCEPTANCE + CHANGE, and DIME retrieves four skill areas.** **D**istress tolerance, **I**nterpersonal effectiveness, **M**indfulness, and **E**motion regulation organize skills taught in DBT. Named skills such as DEAR MAN, TIPP, PLEASE, opposite action, and wise mind are prompts to consult an authorized current manual, not self-explanatory crisis instructions. Comprehensive outpatient DBT is more than a skills list: research protocols commonly coordinate individual therapy, skills training, between-session coaching within defined limits, and a therapist consultation team. A group or app that teaches selected skills may be "DBT-informed" or DBT skills training and should not automatically be represented as the full treatment package. DBT was developed for chronically suicidal people diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and evidence now spans additional populations and adaptations, but efficacy, format, duration, and component evidence differ by problem and setting. It is not the only evidence-supported treatment for borderline presentations or suicide risk. Behavioral target hierarchies, chain analysis, validation, contingency management, commitment strategies, monitoring, and crisis planning are central clinical processes that DIME does not capture. Do not use a mnemonic to coach an acute crisis, promise symptom elimination, or apply advanced methods outside competence. Treatment selection should integrate current evidence, risk, diagnosis and formulation, access, culture, preference, clinician training, fidelity, and response.

memoryAids.title: Type I vs Type II Errors
memoryAids.content: **Decision-error cue:** Type I error rejects a true null under a specified procedure; Type II error fails to reject a false null; power is the probability of rejection under a specified alternative. Alpha does not equal the probability that a reported finding is false, and one minus alpha is not power. Effect size, sample size, variability, design, multiplicity, assumptions, prior evidence, and consequences all shape interpretation.

sourceDetails.whyReputable: This official professional statement directly explains p-values, error control, multiplicity, effect size, uncertainty, and why a threshold alone does not establish importance or truth.

memoryAids.title: Effect-Size Interpretation in Context
memoryAids.content: **Estimate -> Uncertainty -> Context -> Consequence.** Cohen's familiar conventions—d around .20/.50/.80 and r around .10/.30/.50—are historical rough reference points, not universal qualitative labels or conclusions about practical importance. A standardized mean difference depends on the comparison and standardizer; r gives direction and strength of a linear association but does not establish causation; and eta-squared, partial eta-squared, and generalized eta-squared answer different variance questions and should not be mixed. Squaring r is the proportion of variance accounted for only in the relevant simple linear setting, not a universal measure of importance. Interpret an effect against the raw outcome scale, measurement reliability, baseline risk, costs and benefits, duration, comparator, prior evidence in the field, study design, and the smallest effect that would matter. A small effect can be consequential when repeated or applied across a population, and a large standardized effect can be trivial, biased, or imprecise. Report the estimate with a confidence interval or other uncertainty information, specify the effect-size definition, and compare with domain-relevant effects. Statistical significance, effect magnitude, precision, and practical or clinical importance are separate judgments.

sourceDetails.whyReputable: This peer-reviewed methods article directly examines arbitrary benchmark labels, misleading use of squared correlations, cumulative consequences, domain context, and more informative approaches to effect-size interpretation.

Schizophreniform and brief psychotic disorder differ chiefly in course, while delusional disorder and schizoaffective disorder require different symptom and mood relationships. memoryAids.content: **Sensitivity versus criterion:** Signal detection theory models overlapping noise and signal-plus-noise distributions. Sensitivity indexes separation under assumptions; criterion reflects the response threshold shaped by base rate, payoff, instruction, and expectation. A higher hit rate alone cannot establish better sensitivity because false alarms matter. Measures and optimal thresholds depend on the specified model and consequences.

memoryAids.title: Reinforcement Schedules: Application & Extinction Nuance
memoryAids.content: **Decode a schedule with two questions: WHAT advances it, and HOW predictable is the requirement?** **Ratio** schedules advance with responses; **interval** schedules make reinforcement available after time, usually for the first qualifying response after the interval. **Fixed** means a constant requirement and **variable** means requirements vary around a programmed value. Thus FR can produce a postreinforcement pause followed by responding, VR often supports relatively steady responding, FI can produce accelerating or "scalloped" responding, and VI often supports steadier moderate responding under classic laboratory arrangements. These are characteristic patterns, not rankings that every organism, task, or parameter must show. Reinforcer quality, deprivation or satiation, schedule value, instructions, response effort, prior learning, and concurrent alternatives change performance. A weekly paycheck is not automatically FI because salary usually is not delivered contingent on the first response after seven days; identify the actual response-reinforcer contingency. Intermittent reinforcement can produce more responding during extinction than continuous reinforcement in many preparations, but "VR is always most resistant" confuses different definitions and comparison arrangements. Resistance may be measured relative to baseline rate, time, responses, or omitted reinforcers, and those measures can disagree. FVFV is a classification cue, not a universal rate or persistence formula and not an intervention plan.

memoryAids.title: Multicultural Counseling Competencies
memoryAids.content: **A-K-S is the historical cue; add CONTEXT, POWER, and HUMILITY.** The classic multicultural counseling framework organized competence around **A**wareness of one's assumptions and biases, **K**nowledge of the client's worldview and relevant systems, and **S**kills for culturally responsive assessment and intervention. Contemporary APA guidance broadens that retrieval frame: identities are intersectional and situated within ecological, historical, economic, political, and power contexts; people within a named group vary; and the psychologist's own social location affects the encounter. Emic (culture- and context-specific) and etic (cross-context) perspectives are complementary questions, not mutually exclusive answer choices. Cultural humility means continuing self-reflection, openness to correction, and attention to power rather than claiming mastery of a culture. Ask the person how identity, language, community, discrimination, resources, and explanatory models matter; do not infer beliefs from race, ethnicity, nationality, gender, disability, religion, or another label. Adapt methods when supported, evaluate validity for the intended population, use interpreters or consultation appropriately, and document uncertainty. "Choose the culturally sensitive answer" is not a decision rule; collaborative, evidence-informed, context-responsive reasoning is.

memoryAids.title: Cognitive Biases in Clinical Judgment
memoryAids.content: **Use PAUSE as a debiasing routine: Prevalence, Alternatives, Updates, Systems, Evidence.** **Prevalence:** begin with relevant base rates while recognizing that local populations and referral settings change them. **Alternatives:** generate plausible competing explanations and actively seek findings that would differentiate or disconfirm them. **Updates:** revise an initial formulation when new information arrives instead of anchoring on the first label. **Systems:** examine access, culture, language, discrimination, environment, measurement, and team processes before attributing a problem only to the person. **Evidence:** combine validated measures, records, collateral information when appropriate, repeated observation, and explicit reasoning rather than relying on one vivid example. Familiar labels such as anchoring, availability, confirmation bias, hindsight bias, base-rate neglect, attribution error, and illusory correlation are useful hypotheses about judgment, not diagnoses of a clinician's motive or proof that a decision is wrong. Heuristics can be efficient, and merely naming a bias does not reliably remove it. Structured assessment, checklists, statistical tools, consultation, feedback, and deliberate reflection can reduce some errors under some conditions, but each tool has limits and may introduce new ones. Evidence-based practice therefore integrates research with clinical expertise and the person's characteristics, culture, and preferences. PAUSE supports transparent reasoning; it cannot replace competence, a validated instrument, collaborative assessment, or outcome monitoring.

memoryAids.title: Tarasoff: California Case & Historical Rule
memoryAids.content: **TARASOFF is a California case anchor; current jurisdiction controls.** In the 1976 California decision, the court held that when a therapist determines, or under professional standards should determine, that a patient presents a serious danger of violence to another, the therapist must use reasonable care to protect the foreseeable victim. The court described warning the victim or likely intermediaries, notifying police, and other reasonably necessary steps as possibilities whose adequacy depends on the circumstances. It did not create one national formula requiring direct warning whenever a client mentions harm. "Tarasoff I equals warn; Tarasoff II equals protect" is useful history but not a current multistate decision rule. States differ in whether a duty is mandatory, permissive, or not specially codified; covered professionals, triggering language, identifiable-victim requirements, immunity, permitted actions, documentation, and confidentiality rules also differ and can change. Threats involving self-harm, abuse reporting, weapons, forensic roles, schools, or property may invoke different authorities. Ethical confidentiality standards permit disclosure when mandated or permitted by law for a valid purpose, limited to what is necessary; they do not independently settle local duty-to-protect law. When risk emerges, conduct and document a competent individualized assessment, take proportionate safety steps, consult current law and qualified supervisors or counsel when feasible, and disclose only as authorized or required. Do not delay urgent protection while searching for a mnemonic, and do not promise that any single action automatically discharges a legal duty.

memoryAids.content: **Compare behavior and cognition before body size:** Anorexia requires significantly low weight but may include binge-purge behavior. memoryAids.title: Mood Disorders Deep Dive
memoryAids.content: **Mood diagnosis follows episodes and lifetime course:** A major depressive episode requires a sustained cluster including depressed mood or loss of interest plus cognitive, physical, and functional change, but that episode occurs in several disorders. Bipolar I is established by mania; bipolar II requires hypomania plus major depression and no mania; cyclothymia is a chronic subthreshold fluctuation. Hypomania must be an observable departure from baseline, not ordinary energy or productivity, and psychosis or marked severity points away from hypomania. Before labeling unipolar depression, assess prior activation, sleep need, activity, judgment, collateral history, mixed features, seasonality, postpartum timing, substances, medications, thyroid or neurologic causes, grief, trauma, and psychotic symptoms.

memoryAids.title: Competency to Stand Trial
memoryAids.content: **DUSKY asks about present functional ability: CONSULT + UNDERSTAND.** The federal constitutional minimum asks whether the defendant has sufficient present ability to consult with counsel with a reasonable degree of rational understanding and has a rational as well as factual understanding of the proceedings. Competency to stand trial concerns current adjudicative functioning; criminal responsibility or an insanity defense concerns mental state at the time of the alleged offense. A diagnosis, psychosis, intellectual disability, poor legal knowledge, medication status, or unusual behavior alone neither proves nor rules out incompetence. Structured instruments such as the MacCAT-CA can organize observations, but they do not replace jurisdiction-specific law, case facts, collateral information, response-style assessment, and the court's ultimate legal determination. If a defendant is found incompetent, procedure, services, restoration standards, and permissible interventions depend on governing law and individualized findings; restoration is not synonymous with medication. **Jackson v. Indiana** bars indefinite commitment solely because a person is incompetent and requires a reasonable period tied to the probability of attaining competency, followed by ordinary civil process or release when restoration is not foreseeable. Do not promise automatic dismissal or civil commitment. Verify the controlling jurisdiction and forensic role.

memoryAids.content: **Heterogeneous aging:** Processing speed, sensory function, health, social roles, and some memory tasks often change with age, while vocabulary, expertise, emotion regulation, and functioning show varied trajectories. Normal aging is not dementia, disengagement is not inevitable, and cross-sectional age differences can reflect cohort and selection effects. Evaluate change from baseline, daily function, health, medication, culture, opportunity, and supports rather than infer ability from chronological age.

memoryAids.title: Existential Therapy
memoryAids.content: **Existential concerns as inquiry:** Death, freedom and responsibility, isolation, and meaninglessness are Yalom's organizing concerns; Frankl, May, Bugental, and others differ in emphasis. Existential anxiety is not automatically pathology or growth, and meaning is not prescribed by the therapist. The approach relies on phenomenological exploration and relationship rather than a fixed technique set. Safety, diagnosis, culture, spirituality, power, goals, and evidence-supported care remain relevant.

memoryAids.title: Structural Family Therapy - Minuchin
memoryAids.content: **Structural formulation:** Subsystems, boundaries, hierarchy, coalitions, joining, enactment, and restructuring are Minuchin-associated concepts. Enmeshment and disengagement are model-specific relational descriptions, not diagnoses or moral judgments; clearer boundaries are not one universal family form. A family structure does not prove cause of a symptom. Intervention requires assessment of individual needs, safety, coercion, culture, development, power, access, and the family's goals.

memoryAids.title: Gestalt Therapy Techniques
memoryAids.content: **Awareness-oriented experiments:** Empty-chair dialogue, exaggeration, reversal, present-centered inquiry, and attention to figure-ground or contact may deepen awareness when collaboratively chosen. They are not scripts, and changing pronouns or saying "I wont" can misrepresent constraint or blame a client. Unfinished business and contact-boundary terms are theoretical formulations. Consent, pacing, stability, culture, relationship, competence, and observed response govern use.

memoryAids.title: Common Factors in Therapy
memoryAids.content: **Common does not mean identical: remember ALLIANCE = Bond + Goals + Tasks.** Psychotherapy approaches can share relationship, expectancy, empathy, rationale, collaboration, and other contextual processes, and meta-analytic evidence consistently links a stronger working alliance with better outcomes. That association is moderate on average, heterogeneous, and not a simple percentage of causation: improvement can strengthen alliance, patient and therapist factors affect both, and measurement timing matters. The "Dodo bird verdict" is a debated summary of some comparisons among bona fide therapies, not proof that all treatments, techniques, therapists, or doses work equally well for every problem. Delete the 40/30/15/15 pie chart; those slices combine unlike sources of variance and cannot be assigned to an individual case. Specific methods, treatment fidelity and competence, safety needs, diagnosis or problem characteristics, culture, accessibility, patient preference, and therapist effects can all matter alongside common factors. Evidence-based practice integrates the best available research with clinical expertise in the context of the person's characteristics, culture, and preferences. Build and repair alliance, but do not use alliance as a substitute for indicated assessment, an evidence-supported method, outcome monitoring, or referral when competence or response is insufficient.

memoryAids.title: Threats to Internal Validity
memoryAids.content: **Causal alternatives:** History, maturation, testing, instrumentation, selection, attrition, regression, contamination, and interactions can offer rival explanations for change. Random assignment and a concurrent control strengthen causal inference but do not automatically eliminate nonadherence, differential attrition, measurement problems, interference, or analysis bias. Diagnose threats from the actual assignment, timing, measurement, missingness, implementation, and estimand rather than treating "THIS MAID" as a universal checklist solution.

memoryAids.title: Nonparametric Tests
memoryAids.content: **Procedure-specific assumptions remain:** Mann-Whitney, Wilcoxon signed-rank, Kruskal-Wallis, Friedman, Spearman, permutation, and exact tests answer different questions. They are not simply "small-sample ANOVA substitutes" or assumption-free. Independence or pairing, exchangeability, shape, ranking, ties, and sampling design matter. Some target distributions or stochastic ordering rather than medians. Compare estimands and assumptions, report effect sizes and uncertainty, and avoid claiming they are always less powerful.

memoryAids.title: Child Abuse Reporting
memoryAids.content: **Child-abuse reporting is a current-jurisdiction decision process, not one universal rule for every psychologist, role, allegation, or deadline.** Identify the governing jurisdiction, protected child definition, covered reporter and role, reportable conduct, threshold such as reasonable suspicion or cause, source-of-information rules, responsible agency, timing, oral or written follow-up, privilege provisions, emergency duties, and protections or penalties. Many laws do not require proof, and clinicians should not conduct a forensic investigation before a required report, but enough clarifying information may be needed to determine whether the legal threshold is met. Do not promise secrecy, notify a suspected perpetrator automatically, or delay a required report while seeking consultation. Use nonleading, developmentally and culturally responsive communication; address immediate safety; disclose only what law requires or permits; document facts, authority, consultation, timing, actions, and follow-up. Verify current official law and policy rather than memorizing 50-state absolutes.

memoryAids.title: End-of-Life Ethical Issues
memoryAids.content: **Use VALUES + CAPACITY + AUTHORITY + TEAM, not a universal end-of-life checklist.** Advance care planning helps a person discuss goals, values, and treatment preferences for a time when they may be unable to decide. An advance directive may record instructions and/or appoint a health-care agent, but forms, witnessing, activation, revocation, surrogate priority, and scope depend on jurisdiction and setting. **Capacity** is a clinical, decision-specific, and time-specific assessment of abilities such as communicating a choice, understanding relevant information, appreciating its application, and reasoning about options; **competence** is a legal determination. A diagnosis, depression, disability, disagreement, or unconventional choice alone does not establish incapacity, and a stable choice is not always required when values or circumstances legitimately change. Psychologists can support communication, symptom and grief care, family work, team consultation, capacity evaluation within competence, and equitable access to palliative services. APA adopted a resolution on palliative care and end-of-life issues in February 2026, so "APA has no official position" is outdated; that resolution should not be stretched into a single rule about medical aid in dying. Laws and professional roles concerning aid in dying, euthanasia, refusal of treatment, hospice, and surrogate decisions differ. Avoid abandonment, but continuing the same therapy indefinitely is not required: plan transitions and referrals based on need, benefit, consent, competence, safety, and continuity. Kubler-Ross stages describe neither a required sequence nor a treatment plan. Verify current law and policy, collaborate with the person and interdisciplinary team, address culture and access, and document the reasoning.

memoryAids.title: ADHD Presentations: DSM-5-TR Cue
memoryAids.content: **ADHD presentations:** predominantly inattentive, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive, or combined. Diagnosis requires a persistent developmentally inappropriate symptom pattern, several symptoms before age 12, presence in two or more settings, impairment, and consideration of alternative explanations. Thresholds differ for older adolescents/adults. Treatment is individualized and can include behavioral parent/classroom interventions, organizational and skills supports, environmental accommodations, stimulant or nonstimulant medication, and coordinated care. Medication does not “paradoxically calm every hyperactive child,” and no single combination is automatically best for every person.
